fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Year Of Chairs, Queues And Tears", "body": "De Carle spent the year hauling six pressure wave chairs to truth movement festivals, running a ten minute demo program and asking only for donations. He describes eighteen transducers underneath you, a floating sensation he compares to lying on a bed of subwoofers, and an abrupt stop that meditators told him dropped them deeper than twenty years of practice. He recounts a woman who arrived in a wheelchair, barely able to speak, and left sobbing about a daughter she had lost fourteen years earlier. These are his accounts and claims, not verified clinical outcomes."}, {"title": "The Deficiencies He Says Almost Everyone Shares", "body": "Asked what belongs in every cupboard, de Carle names magnesium first, associating shortfalls with cramps, twitches, anxiety, migraines and aching joints, and crediting it with resolving the arthritis that followed his own antibiotic reaction decades ago. He puts sunshine and vitamin D next, then iodine and selenium, arguing that chlorinated and fluoridated water deplete iodine, and connecting low levels to brain fog, dry skin, thyroid trouble and menopausal symptoms. Vitamin C, fulvic trace minerals, B complex and sodium bicarbonate fill out the pack he sells. Everything here is his position rather than settled medical fact."}, {"title": "Children, Formula And The Old Wise Woman", "body": "On raising children, de Carle argues the work begins roughly two years before conception, pointing to older societies where elders knew which foods to feed couples approaching parenthood. He is blunt about supermarket infant formula, claiming that when he last checked he found more ingredients listed in puppy formula than in a leading baby brand, and gestures instead at wet nurses, goats and unpasteurized milk. Chance describes formula samples and coupons arriving unbidden after his daughter was born. Both suggest introducing foods one at a time so a reaction can actually be traced to something."}, {"title": "Detox Traditions, From Turpentine To Suppositories", "body": "The detox stretch moves between de Carle's catalog and old folk practice. He describes albedextrin as something he offers for built up toxic fats, organophosphate residue, cholesterol crystals and the brown marks he calls rancid fat rather than age spots. He says he moved the century old coffee enema and the olive oil liver flush into suppository form because he found the originals ghastly. He recounts turpentine's traditional use against parasites, soaked into sugar as a Trojan horse, while explicitly telling listeners not to rush out and try it. Report only, never instruction."}, {"title": "Everybody Is In Hypnosis All Day", "body": "Underneath the supplements sits a claim about mind. De Carle says the first time he switched off pain he was stuck in heavy traffic with a toothache, visualizing golden light on the tooth at a stranger's suggestion, and the second time he used self hypnosis he had learned. He points to Richard Bandler's work and argues everyone is hypnotized around the clock, most deeply while watching the news and believing it. Chance answers that symbolic literacy is a form of psychic self defense. The same thread runs into de Carle's private members club, built after his videos were pulled in 2014."}]
